headline: The Miami box is a quarter. Allegiant will ask for sixty.
dek: ESPN’s Hard Rock line is 7–7 with Patrick Mahomes 7-of-7 for 95, Kenneth Walker III’s 10-yard opener, and 6:19 of possession; Sunday in Las Vegas is where a 2-0 club has to turn a stub of a road trip into a real AFC West shift.
videoHook: Mahomes didn’t miss. The clock barely moved. Seven-seven in Miami, twenty-nine rushing yards, and now we go to the desert — this is the first full AFC West road Sunday of 2026.
theEdge: DraftKings lays Kansas City -6 on a 45.5 total and ESPN FPI sits at 72.6 percent in Las Vegas, but Polymarket’s 8.6 percent Super Bowl ticket still treats 2-0 as a sample — especially when the last official box is 124 yards and a 7–7 first-quarter board.

storyline.lede: Kansas City is 2-0 in games that actually finished — 31–10 over Denver, 33–30 in overtime over Indianapolis — and then the first road trip of 2026 produced an ESPN box that looks like a quarter, not a verdict. Walker punched the opening score at Hard Rock, Mahomes was perfect on seven throws, Kelce ripped off a 48-yard catch, Ollie Gordon II answered, and the possession clock died at 6:19 to 9:27. That is not an identity. It is a fragment. Week 4 in Las Vegas is where Andy Reid, Eric Bieniemy, and Steve Spagnuolo have to prove the Chiefs can play a full AFC West road game instead of a highlight reel and a shrug.
body: The tape that exists is efficient and thin. Five first downs. Two-for-two on third down. Zero turnovers. Nick Bolton leading the defense with four tackles while Miami’s entire passing game fits in 55 net yards. Pre-game, the pass rush was the open wound after Indianapolis hung 30; the Dolphins sample did not close it, because nobody on that sheet threw enough to measure a rush. Spagnuolo cannot take a 101-yard opponent total into Allegiant and call it a corrective.

Bieniemy’s side has the opposite problem: the downhill look showed up for one snap-sequence — Walker, 10 yards, touchdown — and then vanished into a 29-yard rushing line on five carries. You do not beat a division rival on the road with five designed runs and a perfect passer rating in miniature. The Colts night already proved this offense can grind into overtime. Miami proved it can punch first. Vegas will ask if it can stay on the field.

Availability from the Miami inactives list is the other ghost on the desk. Josh Simmons and Diego Pounds did not dress at tackle, Chamarri Conner was officially out, Jared Wiley sat, and the edge group shuffled Jack Pyburn and Tyreke Smith to inactive after a practice-squad elevation. Until a new report lands, Week 4 is a stress test of tackle depth, safety depth, and whether Cole Christiansen’s elevation was a one-day patch or a tell.

The market is not confused about Sunday. Kansas City is a 6-point road favorite on a 45.5 total, ESPN FPI at 72.6 percent. The long ticket is still cheap at 8.6 percent on Polymarket. That gap is the season in one number: people will fade the Chiefs until the defense posts a full four-quarter night and the run game looks like Week 1 again, not like a five-carry cameo in South Florida.

lastGameReview.label: Week 3 · Sun, Sep 27 · 12:00 PM CT
lastGameReview.lede: At Hard Rock Stadium, the only scoring on the official ESPN sheet is a first-quarter trade: Kenneth Walker III from 10 yards at 12:54 (Harrison Butker kick) and Ollie Gordon II from 3 yards at 3:27 (Riley Patterson kick). Kansas City’s box is 5 first downs, 2-of-2 on third down, 124 total yards, 95 net passing, 29 rushing, 0 turnovers, 6:19 of possession. Miami’s is 7 first downs, 3-of-4 on third, 101 yards, 55 net passing, 46 rushing, 0 turnovers, 9:27 of possession. Combined possession is a quarter. We review the snaps that exist; we do not invent a final that is not on the sheet.

analysis.body: The opening script was Bieniemy in shorthand. Walker’s 10-yard touchdown is the same downhill answer Kansas City used to bury Denver 31–10 in Week 1 and to survive Indianapolis 33–30 in overtime in Week 2: get the back on a track, let the line climb, finish in the red area. Five carries for 29 yards and a score is a successful cameo and a failed volume test. You cannot call that a road-run identity. You can call it proof the first punch still lands.

Mahomes’ 7-of-7 for 95 yards is the cleanest tiny sample a quarterback can post. Travis Kelce’s 1-for-48 is the chunk that makes the 95 look like a real passing game instead of dumpoffs. The problem is first-down math: five Chiefs first downs against seven for Miami, and a possession split that already had Kansas City off the field. Perfect passing on seven attempts does not move a road game if the offense only holds the ball for 6:19. Third down was 2-for-2, which means they converted the only two they saw — and never earned a third one.

Spagnuolo’s unit put up the kind of stat line that looks elite until you remember the clock. Miami 101 total yards, 55 through the air, no turnovers forced, Bolton at four tackles. Gordon’s 3-yard score is a red-zone leak, not a collapse. The pre-game question was the pass rush after it disappeared against Indianapolis; this box cannot answer it. You do not evaluate a front off 55 net passing yards. You evaluate whether the Dolphins were allowed to win first down (7 to 5) and chew the only quarter on the sheet (9:27). That is the warning, not the 101.

The inactives hung over every personnel grouping. Simmons and Pounds out at tackle, Conner out at safety, Wiley out at tight end, Pyburn and Smith out on the edge after Smith had been elevated. If the offense stayed in 11 and leaned on Kelce as the movable chess piece, that is schematic survival, not a full menu. If the defense played without Conner, Bolton’s four tackles are the MIKE doing extra, not a secondary that won the day. Film-room honesty: this was a first-quarter fight with missing pieces, and Allegiant will not honor the sample size.

takeaways.title: The first punch is still Walker
takeaways.body: A 10-yard Walker touchdown on the first road series is the Bieniemy call sheet working on schedule. Five carries is not a plan. Las Vegas is where the back has to see 18–22 touches or the play-action bootleg dies on the vine.

takeaways.title: Mahomes was perfect and almost unemployed
takeaways.body: Seven completions, zero incompletions, 95 yards, Kelce’s 48-yarder as the explosive. That is A-plus efficiency on a C-minus workload. Third down 2-for-2 with only two attempts is the same story: they won the downs they saw and never stayed in the huddle long enough to build a lead.

takeaways.title: The defensive box is a mirage until it isn’t
takeaways.body: One-hundred-one opponent yards will get screenshot. Fifty-five net passing yards will get overread. Gordon still scored from three, Miami still won first downs 7–5, and the pass rush still lacks a full-game temperature check after Indianapolis scored 30.

whatWorked: Walker’s 10-yard opening touchdown — downhill identity on the first road series
Kelce’s 48-yard reception as the only true explosive on the sheet
Third-down efficiency 2-for-2 in the tiny sample
Butker converting the PAT; clean operation in the kicking game
Bolton leading the defense and Miami held to 101 total yards and 55 net pass
whatDidnt: Possession time 6:19 — an offense that never built a drive tree
Only five first downs against Miami’s seven
Rushing volume: 29 yards on five carries after a 10-yard score
Pass rush still unmeasured after the Colts allowed 30; this box does not acquit it
Secondary/tackle depth: Conner, Simmons, and Pounds all inactive, so the personnel answer is incomplete

currentState.lede: The Chiefs are 2-0 in completed games, 7–7 on the only Miami scoring that ESPN printed, and 0-for-1 in proving they can play a full road Sunday. Denver was a statement. Indianapolis was a grind. Miami was a fragment. Week 4 at Las Vegas is the first AFC West road night of 2026, and it will not be graded on a 15-minute clock.

workOn.title: Run-game volume, not run-game vibes
workOn.body: Walker’s touchdown is the look. Five carries is the problem. Bieniemy has to script inside zone and the screen game until Kansas City is winning first down in the desert, or Mahomes will be catching a pass rush that just spent a week hearing it went quiet against Indianapolis.

workOn.title: A full-game pass-rush plan
workOn.body: Spagnuolo cannot file the Dolphins’ 55 net passing yards as evidence the front is back. Simulated pressure and a real four-man temperature check have to show up against a division opponent that will try to make this a slow, physical AFC West tape.

workOn.title: Tackle and safety contingency
workOn.body: Simmons and Pounds inactive, Conner officially out, Wiley down, edge pieces shuffled — that was the Week 3 list. Vegas is the next stress test of whether Kahlil Benson (and whoever is next at safety) can hold up for 60 minutes, not 6:19.

workOn.title: Stay on the field
workOn.body: Two third-down conversions on two attempts is perfect and useless if you only see two. The Colts overtime win was a first-down machine. The Miami box was the opposite. Drive-start and early-down success are the entire Week 4 assignment.

thinkAbout.title: Do we treat Hard Rock as a warning or a stub?
thinkAbout.body: Combined possession of 15:46 is not a football game. It is also not an excuse if the next full tape in Las Vegas looks like five first downs again. The staff has to decide what of that quarter was scheme and what was circumstance.

thinkAbout.title: How loud do we let the Fields noise get?
thinkAbout.body: Adam Schefter has the Giants interested in Justin Fields, and prying him out of Kansas City is a different matter. At 2-0 with Mahomes 7-of-7 on the last sheet, this is a roster-value debate, not a quarterback debate — unless the offensive line depth starts losing games.

thinkAbout.title: Who is the extra receiver if the tackles are in flux?
thinkAbout.body: Cyrus Allen was the pre-Miami name for an expanded route tree. Kelce just posted 48 on one target. If 12 personnel is the protection answer, Allen’s snaps are the first thing that gets squeezed. If 11 is the answer, he has to win the leverage vs. Las Vegas’ second corner.

gamePlan.lede: Week 4 at Las Vegas is the first completed-road exam of the Andy Reid 2026 season: AFC West, CBS, a 6-point favorite on a 45.5 total, ESPN FPI at 72.6 percent. The assignment is to play sixty minutes of Chiefs football after a Miami box that lasted a quarter.
gamePlan.howTheyMatch: Kansas City wants to be a downhill, play-action team with Mahomes creating on the move and Walker finishing. Las Vegas at home will try to turn this into a physical division slog — win early downs, tee off if the Chiefs become two-dimensional, and make a depleted tackle rotation prove it can last. The leverage is simple: if Walker gets volume, the boot and the mesh come alive and Spagnuolo can hunt on his terms. If Kansas City repeats 5 carries / 5 first downs, the Raiders’ rush dictates, and a 6-point road chalk number becomes a trap. Miami was speed and a stub. Vegas is a rival that will make you earn every snap.

keys.title: Feed Walker until the linebackers stop cheating the pass
keys.body: Inside zone from under center is the identity that scored at 12:54 in Miami and buried Denver. Script it early in 12 and 21, then steal the boot when the MIKE steps downhill. Five carries cannot be the feature again.

keys.title: Move Mahomes — don’t plant him
keys.body: Seven-for-seven is what happens when the picture is clean. Play-action boot and a living pocket keep Las Vegas from pinning their ears back. Kelce as the first read on the move is the Miami 48-yarder, translated to a full game.

keys.title: Manufacture a pass rush; don’t wait for one
keys.body: The Colts night went quiet. The Dolphins night didn’t throw enough to count. Spagnuolo’s simulated pressure — show heat, drop a lineman, bring Bolton or a nickel — has to create the negative plays a four-man rush has not documented since Week 1.

keys.title: Take away the shot, rally to tackle
keys.body: Cover-2 shell on obvious passing downs, especially if Conner’s absence carries any residual usage in the safety room. Bolton is the rally player (4 tackles on the last sheet). Do not give Las Vegas the one explosive that turns a 6-point favorite into a street fight.

keys.title: Protect the tackle spots like they’re the game
keys.body: Simmons and Pounds did not play in Miami. Fans already wanted Benson starting. Chip with Walker, keep a tight end in, and do not ask Mahomes to win a dropback contest against a division edge in a loud building.

script: Open in 21/12: under-center inside zone to Walker, same family as the 10-yard Miami score, win the first two first downs.
Second series: play-action boot off the zone fake, Kelce as the moving read, Mahomes on the perimeter.
Vs. man: mesh with Kelce and a receiver crossing, Walker as the checkdown so the 7-of-7 efficiency has an outlet.
When Las Vegas’ ends climb: Walker spacing screen, let the offensive line get to space, punish the same aggressive rush that just spent a week hearing about Indianapolis.
Third-and-medium: Spagnuolo simulated pressure, Bolton timing the add, a lineman dropping — do not live on a four-man that went quiet in Week 2.
Late-down shell: Cover-2, two deep, five under, rally. Make Las Vegas drive the length of the field instead of ending the 6-point chalk on one shot.

nextGame.label: Week 4 · Sun, Oct 4 · 3:25 PM CT
nextGame.note: First AFC West road Sunday of 2026: 2-0 on completed games, a 7–7 Miami fragment on the last sheet, and a 6-point favorite that still has to prove it can play a full sixty.

spotlight.title: Perfect, and almost unused
spotlight.body: Mahomes’ 7-of-7 for 95 yards is a laboratory result, not a game. Kelce’s 48-yarder was the only explosive. Vegas is where the dropback count has to rise without the completion percentage falling off a cliff.

spotlight.title: Walker is the feature until he isn’t
spotlight.body: Ten-yard touchdown, 29 yards on five carries. That is a back waiting for a coordinator to trust the run after the first score. Bieniemy’s entire play-action menu in Allegiant hangs on whether Walker sees real volume.

spotlight.title: The rush still owes a full tape
spotlight.body: Pre-Miami, the local desk was already saying the pass rush disappeared in Week 2 and had a chance to get right against the Dolphins. Fifty-five net passing yards did not settle the argument. Spagnuolo’s first true temperature check is now a division opponent at home.

spotlight.title: The tackle room is the quiet crisis
spotlight.body: Simmons and Pounds inactive, fan support for Kahlil Benson starting, and a road division game next. If that pair is still in flux, chips, tight ends, and boots are not window dressing — they are the protection plan.

spotlight.title: Conner’s absence changes the shell
spotlight.body: Chamarri Conner officially ruled out in Miami is a real secondary problem even if the opponent only threw for 55. Cover-2 and rally-to-tackle become more attractive if that safety room is still patching.

spotlight.title: Fields is an asset, not a quarterback controversy
spotlight.body: The Giants may want Justin Fields; getting him out of Kansas City is another matter. At 2-0 with Mahomes healthy, this is cap-and-roster leverage, and it should stay in the background unless the line play forces a different conversation.

spotlight.title: London is a fan stop, Vegas is the job
spotlight.body: Chiefs House hits Leicester Square on October 2–3. The football calendar hits Allegiant on October 4. The Kingdom can do both; the roster only gets graded on one.

matchups.unit: Walker / Bieniemy zone vs. Raiders front seven
matchups.chiefs: Kenneth Walker III, under-center inside zone
matchups.note: Walker already scored from 10 on the road and the Chiefs just posted a 31–10 opener on the ground identity. Volume is the only question; the look has been winning.

matchups.opponent: Las Vegas secondaries / linebackers in man
matchups.note: 7-of-7 and a 48-yard Kelce shot is a tiny sample with a loud implication: if Las Vegas sits man, mesh and the boot are live. If they sit two-deep, the checkdowns and Walker have to cash.

matchups.unit: Chiefs tackles vs. Raiders edge rush
matchups.chiefs: Tackle rotation (Simmons/Pounds inactive in Wk 3; Benson in the conversation)
matchups.note: The last official availability list left two tackles in street clothes on the road. A division edge in a loud building is exactly how a 6-point favorite becomes uncomfortable.

matchups.unit: Spagnuolo front vs. Raiders pass protection
matchups.note: Quiet against Indianapolis, unmeasured against Miami’s 55-yard passing line. Until the rush posts a full-game negative-play count, this is not a Chiefs edge — it is a to-do list.

matchups.unit: Bolton / box vs. Raiders early-down run
matchups.chiefs: Nick Bolton (4 tackles last sheet) and the MIKE level
matchups.note: Miami won first downs 7–5 and possessed 9:27 of the only quarter on the sheet. If Las Vegas copies that early-down math, Bolton has to be the eraser.

xsandos.title: Walker downhill, same family as the Hard Rock opener
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10, opening script @ Las Vegas, 21 or 12 personnel
xsandos.why: Walker’s only official road snaps this season include a 10-yard touchdown and a 29-yard line on five carries. Bieniemy has to re-establish the under-center zone look that scored at 12:54 in Miami and underpinned the 31–10 Denver win, or the Raiders’ front will ignore the run and hunt a tackle rotation that just sat Simmons and Pounds.
xsandos.coaching: Walker: one cut, no bounce into the edge unless the shade gives it. Interior line: zone steps, climb to the second level, finish. Reid/Bieniemy: do not check out of this after one gain — the Miami mistake was ending the feature at five carries.

xsandos.title: Boot off the Walker fake — put Mahomes on the boundary
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-medium after a live zone run, 12 personnel @ Allegiant
xsandos.why: Mahomes was 7-of-7 when the picture was clean; Kelce just took a 48-yarder. Play-action boot sells the same inside-zone that scored in Miami, moves the launch point, and keeps a Raiders edge from teeing off on a tackle group that was already down two bodies last week.
xsandos.coaching: Mahomes: sell the fake, get the shoulders around, first read Kelce on the move. Kelce: delay a beat, then climb to the numbers. Backside tackle/TE: hinge, do not chase upfield. This is protection-by-movement, not a dropback dare.

xsandos.title: Mesh to cash man and keep the 7-of-7 alive
xsandos.why: Kelce is the mismatch if Las Vegas sits man to take away the shot after watching a 48-yard clip. Mesh manufactures a rub for Kelce, gives Mahomes the easy throw he did not miss in Miami, and parks Walker as the outlet so the offense does not repeat a 5-first-down possession tree.
xsandos.coaching: Kelce: win the traffic, do not dance. Slot/X: tight mesh, pick without hunting. Walker: checkdown in Mahomes’ vision immediately — the Miami sample had zero incompletions because the answers were on time. Bieniemy: if they switch the mesh, sit and throw the option route, don’t force the crossing ball.

xsandos.title: Walker screen when the ends climb
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10 or 2nd-and-long vs. an upfield Raiders rush, 11 personnel
xsandos.why: The local pass-rush conversation has been about Kansas City’s front going quiet — Las Vegas will assume the inverse and let their ends climb. A Walker spacing screen turns that aggression into the missing rushing volume (29 yards last sheet) and protects a tackle rotation that just inactive-listed Simmons and Pounds.
xsandos.coaching: Mahomes: hitch and get it out, no hero ball. Walker: set the rush, then get north. Pulling linemen: climb to the second level, don’t hunt the first color. This is how you punish a division edge without asking a backup tackle to win a 40-yard dropback.

labels.te: release to the second level / wall

xsandos.title: Spags two-deep: no cheap shots in a loud building
xsandos.situation: Obvious passing downs / 2nd-and-long @ Allegiant, especially with Conner out of the Miami 11
xsandos.why: Kansas City just allowed a 3-yard Gordon score but only 55 net passing yards — the next opponent will try the explosive, not the grind, if they smell a safety room patching for Chamarri Conner. Cover-2 takes away the shot that wrecks a 6-point road favorite and lets Bolton (4 tackles) rally.
xsandos.coaching: Safeties: split the post, nothing over the top. Corners: funnel and force the checkdown. Bolton: you are the rally tackler, same job you posted in Miami. Spagnuolo: do not get greedy with zero-blitz in a division building until the four-man has actually won a snap on this tape.

xsandos.title: Simulated heat: manufacture the rush the Colts tape didn’t
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-7 or 3rd-and-4, early-to-mid possession vs. Las Vegas protection
xsandos.why: The pass rush vanished against Indianapolis and never got a real sample against Miami’s 55-yard passing line. Spagnuolo’s signature — show five or six, drop a lineman, bring a second-level adder — is how you create negative plays without asking a four-man that has not documented a full-game win since Week 1.
xsandos.coaching: Show nickel pressure, drop the end into the hook, time Bolton’s add off the guard’s helmet. Secondary: you are in a three-under/three-deep family behind it, not a dare. If Conner’s absence is still dictating safety usage, do not rotate into a look that isolates a backup on a vertical. Win the down; do not hunt a poster sack.

coaching.topic: Andy Reid vs. a division road Sunday
coaching.detail: Reid’s first 2026 road trip produced a quarter-sized ESPN box. The Hall of Fame answer in Allegiant is not a new philosophy — it is finishing the script he started with Walker at 12:54 and refusing to live in a seven-dropback sample.

coaching.topic: Eric Bieniemy’s downhill identity needs a full menu
coaching.detail: The OC has the look (Walker TD, zone family) and not the volume (five carries). Vegas is where 12 personnel, inside zone, and the boot have to live together for four quarters, not one series.

coaching.topic: Steve Spagnuolo still owes a pass-rush night
coaching.detail: Thirty points allowed to Indianapolis is the real defensive problem; 101 yards in a Miami fragment is not the solution. Simulated pressure plus a Cover-2 late-down shell is the grown-up call sheet until the four-man proves it again.

injuries.note: Officially ruled out for the Dolphins game; safety room was already in a patch-and-rally mode on the last official 11.
Did not play at tackle vs. Miami; the first item on the Week 4 protection board until a new report.
Inactive at tackle alongside Simmons for the Dolphins matchup.
Tight end inactive vs. Miami, thinning the 12-personnel menu on the last official list.
Defensive end inactive vs. Miami; part of an edge group that was already under the microscope after Week 2.
Elevated from the practice squad Saturday, then listed among those who would not play Sunday.

personnel.detail: Linebacker elevated from the practice squad with the linebacker room already thin; a one-week patch that becomes a tell if he is back up for Las Vegas.
The club elevated the defensive end and still kept him out of the Dolphins 11 — edge depth is in flux heading into a division game.
Nussmeier was listed as the third QB vs. Miami. Operational note, not a controversy, with Mahomes 7-of-7 on the last sheet.
Week 3 fan polling backed Benson in the starting mix at a moment two tackles were already inactive. That debate travels to Allegiant whether the staff says it out loud or not.
Adam Schefter has New York circling Fields; Kansas City has no football reason to move a backup at 2-0 unless the return is a protection or depth piece that actually helps Sunday.

Pre-Miami argument was that Allen deserved a bigger route tree. One Kelce explosive and a thin first-down count means his Week 4 usage is the tell on whether Reid is 11-personnel aggressive or 12-personnel protective.

strategies: Script Walker inside zone for the first two series in Allegiant until Las Vegas’ linebackers stop cheating the pass.
Boot Mahomes off that fake — protection by movement for a tackle rotation that just sat Simmons and Pounds.
Use mesh vs. man so Kelce’s 48-yard Miami clip becomes a full-game diet, not a one-off.
Walker spacing screens when Raiders ends climb; steal the rushing yards the Miami box never accumulated.
Spagnuolo: simulated pressure on early downs, Cover-2 on late downs — stop waiting for a four-man rush that went quiet in Week 2.
Chip and 12-personnel protection until the tackle report is clean; do not drop back 40 times in a division building on a 6-point road number.
debates: Is the Miami ESPN box a weather-stub to ignore or a 5-first-down warning to panic over?
Has Spagnuolo’s pass rush actually been fixed, or did Miami simply not throw enough to measure it?
If Simmons and Pounds are still in flux, is Benson the answer or is 12 personnel the answer?
Should Kansas City even take a call on Justin Fields at 2-0, or is that noise for a 6–11 hangover?
Do you want more Cyrus Allen, or do you want Kelce and Walker to eat every snap until the first-down math looks like Week 1?

runOfShow.talkTrack: Mahomes didn’t miss. The clock barely moved. 7–7 at Hard Rock, 124 yards, 6:19 of possession — and now we go to Vegas. No fake fourth quarter. Here’s the tape that exists.
Walker 10-yard opener, Gordon answers from 3, Kelce 48, Mahomes 7-of-7. First-down math (5 vs. 7) and the possession split. What the 101 defensive yards do and do not prove.
Simmons, Pounds, Conner, Wiley, the edge shuffle. Christiansen elevated. What of that list we still don’t know for Sunday, and what we refuse to invent.
Denver 31–10, Indianapolis 33–30 OT, Miami fragment. What Bieniemy must volume-up, what Spagnuolo still owes, why the long ticket is only 8.6 percent.
Allegiant, CBS, KC -6 / 45.5, FPI 72.6. Walker volume, boot, mesh, screens. Cover-2 and zone blitz. Tackle protection as the real game.
Six calls: inside zone, boot, mesh, Walker screen, Cover-2, simulated pressure. Name the players. Tie every card to this week, not a generic menu.
Favorite, not a coronation. 72.6 percent is a good bet on a full game. 8.6 percent to win it all is the market saying 2-0 plus a 7–7 stub is still a sample.
The Kingdom can do London on Friday. The roster has to do sixty minutes in the desert on Sunday. We’ll see you after the tape.
